skill.name: ppt-orchestra-skill
skill.description: Plan and orchestrate multi-slide PowerPoint decks with slide type classification, layout variety, typography rules, compilation guidance, and text-based QA checks.
skill.summary: Plan structured PowerPoint decks with consistent design rules and QA checks.
skill.author: MiniMax-AI

security_audit.summary: All static alerts were false positives caused by Markdown inline code, fenced examples, and local build or QA commands. The reviewed skill shows no prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or unauthorized network behavior.

static_findings.snippet: - **Don't forget text box padding** — when aligning lines or shapes with text edges, set `margin: 0`
After all slide JS files are generated in `slides/`, create `slides/compile.js` to compile them into
1. Generate slides → Extract text with `python -m markitdown output.pptx` → Review content
- 2x2 or 2x3 grid (image on one side, grid of content blocks on other)
- **Don't create text-only slides** — add images, icons, charts, or visual elements; avoid plain tit
- **Don't use low-contrast elements** — icons AND text need strong contrast against the background;

content.value_statement: Large decks often drift in structure, style, and quality during generation. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a repeatable plan for slide types, design rules, compilation, and QA.
actual_capabilities: Classifies every slide as a cover, table of contents, divider, content page, or closing page.
Defines layout choices for text, images, comparisons, timelines, data visuals, and summary slides.
Sets typography, spacing, contrast, and visual variety rules for consistent deck design.
Provides a local pptxgenjs compilation pattern for generated slide files.
Adds text-based QA steps with MarkItDown and placeholder checks before final delivery.
limitations: It guides deck planning and orchestration, but it does not create the final PPTX by itself.
The compile example must be adjusted for the actual slide count and project paths.
It assumes access to pptxgenjs and MarkItDown when compilation and QA are required.
Text extraction cannot catch every layout, spacing, image, or contrast problem.

use_cases.title: Structure a client presentation
use_cases.description: Plan a clear deck outline with varied slide types, consistent formatting, and review steps before client delivery.

use_cases.title: Coordinate product update slides
use_cases.description: Turn roadmap notes, metrics, and decisions into a structured deck with data slides and closing actions.

use_cases.title: Automate PPTX generation
use_cases.description: Use the compile and QA guidance to manage generated slide files and verify extracted deck text.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a new deck
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ppt-orchestra-skill to plan a 10-slide deck about [topic] for [audience]. Classify each slide and suggest layout direction.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this deck outline with ppt-orchestra-skill. Identify repeated layouts, weak slide types, missing visuals, and needed QA checks.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate slide generation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ppt-orchestra-skill to assign slide types, theme rules, typography, spacing, and QA expectations before generating each slide file.

prompt_templates.title: Run a QA pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply ppt-orchestra-skill after generation. Extract deck text, list content issues, find placeholders, and define fixes before final approval.

output_examples.input: Plan a 12-slide investor update for a SaaS company.
output: A slide-by-slide plan with cover, agenda, section dividers, metric pages, roadmap content, and closing actions.
Design guidance for fonts, margins, visual variety, chart placement, and source labels.
A QA checklist covering missing content, placeholders, typos, and follow-up review.

output_examples.input: Review an outline that uses bullet slides for every section.
output: Recommendations to replace repeated bullet slides with comparisons, timelines, data visuals, and image-led layouts.
Specific warnings about weak contrast, small titles, centered body text, and inconsistent spacing.

output_examples.input: Prepare a workflow for generating slides as separate files.
output: A local compilation approach for combining slide files into one presentation.
A verification loop that extracts text, checks placeholders, fixes issues, and repeats review.

best_practices: Set slide count, theme colors, font pairing, and section structure before generating individual slides.
Vary layouts across the deck while keeping margins, spacing, and typography consistent.
Run text extraction and visual review after fixes, because one correction can introduce another issue.
anti_patterns: Using the same title-and-bullets layout for most content slides.
Declaring the deck finished after the first render without a fix-and-verify cycle.
Installing global dependencies in shared environments without approval or version review.

faq.question: Does this skill create the PowerPoint file directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides planning, orchestration, compile guidance, and QA rules for generated PPTX workflows.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What dependencies does the skill mention?
faq.answer: It references pptxgenjs for PPTX creation and MarkItDown for text extraction during QA.

faq.question: Can it help with an existing outline?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review an outline for slide type balance, repeated layouts, missing visuals, and QA gaps.

faq.question: How does it improve presentation quality?
faq.answer: It enforces slide classification, visual variety, typography rules, spacing rules, and repeated content review.

faq.question: Is any security issue confirmed in the audit?
faq.answer: No confirmed issue was found. The static alerts were Markdown examples and local workflow commands.
